column10: notes

802.3ba approved by IEEE-SA SB 17 Jun 2010 (covers 40 AND 100GbE). S4810 announced Nov 2010 'shipping by end of this quarter' (secondary; planned ship). Mellanox SX1036/SwitchX 40GbE reached market May 2011 (The Register; secondary).

column7: Juniper T1600 100GbE PIC / Alcatel-Lucent 7750 SR 100GbE IMM
column10: Same standard and date as 40GbE. Router interfaces announced 2009 with commercial availability planned H1/mid-2010 (secondary); actual first-ship date not confirmed. First 100GbE server NICs (e.g. Mellanox ConnectX-4) are later (2014-2015) and not verified here.

802.3bs approved 6 Dec 2017 (IEEE task-force page). Also later 802.3cd (50G lanes). Tomahawk 3 silicon shipping to qualified customers Dec 2017; first systems Oct 2018 (same basis as 400GbE row). 200GbE was not a distinct ML-cluster generation; optional row.

Standard approved 6 Dec 2017. Tomahawk 3 switch silicon shipping to qualified customers 19 Dec 2017; first shipping 400GbE systems (Arista 7060X4) Oct 2018; TH3 production-qualified 24 Oct 2018. Use 2017 if counting silicon.

802.3df approved 16 Feb 2024 (task-force page; IEEE Xplore pub 15 Mar 2024). Products preceded the IEEE standard (built to the Ethernet Technology Consortium 800GBASE-R spec, not verified here). TH5 sampled Aug 2022; production volume Mar 2023. NVIDIA Spectrum-X800 announced Mar 2024 for 2025 availability.

column7: Mellanox ConnectX-3 adapter / SwitchX SX6036 switch
column10: Raw 4x14.0625 Gb/s = 56.25 Gb/s; 64b/66b -> ~54.5 Gb/s data (6.8 GB/s). IBTA Vol 2 Release 1.3 (Nov 2012) is the first spec release found carrying FDR 56 Gb/s; products preceded it. ConnectX-3 announced Jun 2011; GA Q3-Q4 2011 (secondary).

spec_year left blank: Vol 2 R1.3 (Nov 2012) only 'lays the groundwork for EDR... expected 2013-2014'; Vol 2 R1.3.1 (29 Nov 2016) updates EDR electrical requirements. No single EDR spec release found. Switch-IB unveiled Jun 2014; systems 'available for orders' Nov 2014.

IBTA Vol 1/2 Release 1.4 (21 Apr 2020) adds 50 Gb/s-per-lane PAM4 (the HDR lane rate); products preceded the spec. Mellanox announced HDR Nov 2016 (SC16) with GA promised for 2017; Mellanox Feb 2019 release says HDR shipments began Q4 2018.
IBTA Vol 1 Release 1.5 (18 Aug 2021) adds NDR 400 Gb/s; final NDR physical specs in Vol 2 R1.5 (Oct 2023). Quantum-2 'now available' 9 Nov 2021; ConnectX-7 'will sample in January' (2022).

IBTA Vol 1 Release 1.7 (5 Oct 2023) first defines XDR (200 Gb/s per lane). Quantum-X800 announced 18 Mar 2024 for availability 'next year'; NVIDIA dev blog 18 May 2025 says ConnectX-8 'now in full production' in HGX B300/GB300 NVL72. 2024 = announcement year only.
Bidirectional 160 GB/s (1280 Gb/s) = 4 links x 40 GB/s bidir (20 GB/s per direction per link). Announced Apr 2016; GA in DGX-1 Jun 2016.
Bidirectional 300 GB/s (2400 Gb/s) = 6 links x 50 GB/s bidir. Announced May 2017; 10-Q for FY18 Q2 (quarter ended Jul 2017) says NVIDIA 'announced and began shipping' V100.
Bidirectional 600 GB/s (4800 Gb/s) = 12 links x 25 GB/s per direction. Announced and shipping May 2020 (launch-release wording not re-fetched here).
Bidirectional 900 GB/s (7200 Gb/s) = 18 links. Announced Mar 2022; 'full production' 20 Sep 2022; FY23 Q3 release (quarter ended 30 Oct 2022) says NVIDIA 'began shipping' H100.

Bidirectional 1.8 TB/s (14400 Gb/s) per GPU (18 links). Announced 18 Mar 2024. Samples in FY25 Q2; first revenue quarter = FY25 Q4 (28 Oct 2024 - 26 Jan 2025) 'billions of dollars in sales in its first quarter'. 2024 is the best single year but could be argued as 2025 for volume.

column7: Intel Xeon E5-2600 (Mar 2012) / AMD Radeon HD 7970 (retail 9 Jan 2012)
column10: 8 GT/s x16 with 128b/130b encoding: 128 Gb/s raw -> 126.0 Gb/s = 15.75 GB/s per direction. Base 3.0 released to members 18 Nov 2010 (PCI-SIG release via reprint). HD 7970 launched 22 Dec 2011 but retail Jan 2012; Mellanox ConnectX-3 (PCIe 3.0 adapter) announced Jun 2011.

16 GT/s x16 128b/130b: 256 Gb/s raw -> 252.1 Gb/s = 31.51 GB/s. Spec 4.0 v1.0 released Oct 2017 (secondary reports; PCI-SIG site not fetchable). AC922 4-GPU air-cooled GA 22 Dec 2017 per IBM; IBM calls POWER9 first chip with PCIe Gen4.

column7: Intel 12th Gen Core (Alder Lake) desktop / IBM POWER10 E1080
column10: 32 GT/s x16 128b/130b: 512 Gb/s raw -> 504.1 Gb/s = 63.02 GB/s (PCI-SIG quotes 128 GB/s bidirectional). Spec released 29 May 2019 (PCI-SIG release reprint). Alder Lake on sale 4 Nov 2021 (secondary for date). Datacenter: Sapphire Rapids/H100 PCIe later (2022-2023), not verified here.

column7: NVIDIA ConnectX-8 SuperNIC (integrated PCIe Gen6 switch) in HGX B300 / GB300 NVL72
column10: 64 GT/s PAM4 with 1b/1b FLIT encoding: 1024 Gb/s = 128 GB/s per direction before FLIT/FEC/CRC overhead (~121 GB/s payload if 242 of 256 flit bytes carry TLP data; derived not sourced). Spec released 11 Jan 2022. ConnectX-8 'now in full production' per NVIDIA blog 18 May 2025; earliest shipping Gen6 product found, earlier ones not ruled out.

128 GT/s PAM4 1b/1b FLIT: 2048 Gb/s = 256 GB/s per direction before FLIT overhead (512 GB/s bidirectional). Spec finalized and released to members Jun 2025 (secondary; PCI-SIG site not fetchable). first_product_year blank: no shipping product confirmed.
